questions.q: Choose the correct statement regarding GIFT to overcome infertility.
options: Ova collected from a female donor are transferred to the uterus of an infertile female.
Early embryos with up to $8$ blastomeres are transferred to the uterus of an infertile female.
Early embryos with up to $8$ blastomeres are transferred into the fallopian tube of an infertile female.
It is the transfer of an ovum collected from a donor into the fallopian tube of another female who cannot produce ovum but can provide suitable environment for fertilization and development.
questions.solution:
GIFT stands for Gamete Intra Fallopian Transfer.

It is an assisted reproductive technology used to overcome infertility in females who cannot produce an ovum.

In this method, an ovum collected from a donor is transferred into the fallopian tube of the recipient female.

The recipient female cannot produce an ovum but can provide a suitable environment for fertilization and further embryonic development.

Answer: It is the transfer of an ovum collected from a donor into the fallopian tube of another female who cannot produce ovum but can provide suitable environment for fertilization and development.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The method of directly of injecting a sperm into ovum in assisted reproductive technology is called :
questions.solution:
Intra cytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI) is a specialized procedure in assisted reproductive technology (ART) where a single sperm is directly injected into the cytoplasm of an ovum to facilitate fertilization.

Embryo transfer (ET) involves transferring an embryo into the uterus or fallopian tube.

Gamete intra fallopian transfer (GIFT) involves the transfer of an ovum collected from a donor into the fallopian tube of another female who cannot produce one, but can provide suitable environment for fertilization.

Zygote intra fallopian transfer (ZIFT) involves the transfer of a zygote or early embryo (up to 8 blastomeres) into the fallopian tube.

Answer: Intra cytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI)

Zygote intra fallopian transfer (ZIFT) involves the transfer of a zygote or early embryo (up to 8 blastomeres) into the fallopian tube.

Answer: Intra cytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI)

questions.solution:
The sexually transmitted infections (STI) or venereal diseases (VD) or reproductive tract infections (RTI) are infections or diseases which are transmitted through sexual intercourse. Among these, HIV infection is most dangerous which is caused by retrovirus.

Except for hepatitis-B, genital herpes and HIV infections, other diseases like Gonorrhoea, etc. are completely curable if detected early and treated properly. Gonorrhoea is caused by a bacterium, Neisseria gonorrhoeae, which infects the mucous membranes of the reproductive tract, including the cervix, uterus, and fallopian tubes in female and the urethra in women and men.

ZYGOTE INTRA-FALLOPIAN TRANSFER (ZIFT): It is also one of the assisted methods of conception. The procedure for ZIFT is similar to IVF-ET. In this method, after In-vitro fertilization, the zygote is transferred into the fallopian tube. After the transfer of the zygote early stages of development, implantation, and maintenance of pregnancy take place in the normal method.

The embryo is transformed directly into the uterus for implantation and further development. Embryos formed by In-vivo fertilization could be used for such transfer to assist those females who fail to conceive.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Select the hormone-releasing Intra-Uterine Devices.
questions.solution:
INTRAUTERINE DEVICE (IUDs): These are small mechanical devices made up of plastic, copper or stainless steel. They are in the form of loop, coil, T or 7 shaped. IUD is inserted into the uterus of the female by an experienced gynaecologist. It could remain inside the uterus for up to 3 years. IUD prevents implantation of the blastocyst and prevents conception. It is a reliable method of birth control.
There are 3 forms of IUDs:
i) Non-medicated IUDs: These IUDs phagocytes sperms within the uterus. Ex: Lippes loop.
ii) Copper releasing IUDs: These IUDs release copper ions within the uterus which decrease the sperm motility and suppress the fertilizing capacity of sperms. E.g. Copper-T (CuT), Copper-7 (Cu7), multiload 375 etc.
iii) Hormone releasing IUDs: These IUDs release hormones which make the uterus unsuitable for implantation and cervix hostile for sperms. E.g. Progestasert, LNG-20 (levonorgestrel 20).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following sexually transmitted diseases is not completely curable?
questions.solution: Herpes simplex type 1 or 2 viruses causes genital herpes, an infection of the skin and mucous membranes in the genital and surrounding areas. Herpes simplex virus usually spreads, when in contact with blisters. However, people with genital herpes can shed the virus from the genital area and infect others even without a blister being present. Cold sores on the mouth are a potential source of genital infection during mouth-to-genital contact. Medications can help decrease the severity of the herpes lesions and prevent recurrences, but they do not cure the infection.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding sexually transmitted discases (STDs)?
options: A person may contact syphilis by sharing milk with one already suffering from the disease.
Haemophilia is one of the STDs.
Genital herpes and sickle-cell anaemia are both STDs.
The chances of a 5-years boy contacting a SID are very little.
questions.solution:
The chances of a 5 years boy contacting STD are very little. However, it is not impossible entirely, as STD does not only spread through sexual contact. It spreads through body fluids. A person cannot contact STD by sharing milk with infected person, as STD does not spread by a mere touch. However, risk of infection increases when the noninfected person comes in contact with sores on the body of infected person. Haemophilia is not a STD, but X-linked recessive disease. Sickle cell anaemia is autosomal recessive disorder.
Related Theory
Reproductive health is a state of complete physical, mental and social well-being and not merely the absence of disease relating to the reproductive system and its functions and process, while Reproductive fitness is the individual's reproductive success (equal to average contribution to gene pool).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The test-tube baby programme employs which one of the following techniques?
questions.solution: The test-tube baby programme employs the technique of in vitro fertilization (IVF) and zygote intrafallopian transfer (ZIFT) technique. ZIFT is a method used to treat infertility, in which an egg fertilized in vitro (outside the body) is placed into a woman's fallopian tube (oviduct). It is an assisted reproductive procedure similar to IVF and embryo transfer, the difference being that zygote or proembryo is transferred into the fallopian tube, instead of the uterus. Because the fertilized egg (zygote) is directly transferred into the tubes, the procedure is also referred to as tubal embryo transfer.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: In vitro fertilization is a technique that involves transfer of which one of the following into the Fallopian tube?
options: Either zygote or early embryo upto 8 cell stage
questions.solution: In vitro fertilization (IVF) or test-tube baby technique involves fertilizing one or more eggs outside the body and then transferring the fertilized eggs known as pre-embryos back into the uterus. Zygote Intra Fallopian Transfer (ZIFT) is an example of IVF. In this, the zygote or early embryos upto 8 blastomeres are transferred into the Fallopian tube. If the embryo has more than 8 blastomeres then it is transferred into uterus called as IUT.

options: detecting sex of the unborn foetus
transfer of embryo into the uterus of a surrogate mother
questions.solution:
Amniocentesis is a technique for the diagnosis of congenital abnormalities before birth. By karyotypic studies of somatic cells, abnormalities due to changes in chromosome number like Down's syndrome, Turner's syndrome, Klinefelter's syndrome, etc, can be determined.
It can be used as a pre-natal diagnostic technique. These days, amniocentesis is being misused also. Mothers even get their normal foetus aborted if it is a female.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: What does the term 'Reproductive Health' primarily refer to?
options: The absence of diseases in reproductive organs
Healthy reproductive organs with normal functions
questions.solution: Reproductive Health simply refers to healthy reproductive organs with normal functions. However, it has a broader perspective and includes the emotional and social aspects of reproduction also. According to the World Health Organisation (WHO), Reproductive Health means a total well-being in all aspects of reproduction, i.e., physical, emotional, behavioural and social. Therefore, a society with people having physically and functionally normal reproductive organs and normal emotional and behavioural interactions among them in all sex-related aspects might be called reproductively healthy.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which country was among the first to initiate national action plans and programs for Reproductive Health?
questions.solution: India was amongst the first countries in the world to initiate action plans and programmes at a national level to attain total Reproductive Health as a social goal. These programmes called ‘family planning’ were initiated in 1951 and were periodically assessed over the past decades. Improved programmes covering wider reproduction-related areas are currently in operation under the popular name ‘Reproductive and Child Health Care (RCH) programmes’. Creating awareness among people about various reproduction related aspects and providing facilities and support for building up a reproductively healthy society are the major tasks under these programmes.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which mediums are used by governmental and non-governmental agencies to create awareness about reproduction-related aspects?
questions.solution: With the help of audio-visual and the print-media governmental and non-governmental agencies have taken various steps to create awareness among the people about reproduction-related aspects. Parents, other close relatives, teachers and friends, also have a major role in the dissemination of the above information. Introduction of sex education in schools should also be encouraged to provide right information to the young so as to discourage children from believing in myths and having misconceptions about sex-related aspects. Proper information about reproductive organs, adolescence and related changes, safe and hygienic sexual practices, sexually transmitted diseases (STD), AIDS, etc., would help people, especially those in the adolescent age group to lead a reproductively healthy life. Educating people, especially fertile couples and those in marriageable age group, about available birth control options, care of pregnant mothers, post-natal care of the mother and child, importance of breast feeding, equal opportunities for the male and the female child, etc., would address the importance of bringing up socially conscious healthy families of desired size.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: In what year did India’s population cross the 1 billion mark?
questions.solution: In the last century an all-round development in various fields significantly improved the quality of life of the people. However, increased health facilities along with better living conditions had an explosive impact on the growth of population. The world population which was around 2 billion (2000 million) in 1900 rocketed to about 6 billion by 2000 and 7.2 billion in 2011. A similar trend was observed in India too. Our population which was approximately 350 million at the time of our independence reached close to the billion mark by 2000 and crossed 1.2 billion in May 2011. A rapid decline in death rate, maternal mortality rate (MMR) and infant mortality rate (IMR) as well as an increase in number of people in reproducible age are probable reasons for this. Through our Reproductive Child Health (RCH) programme, though we could bring down the population growth rate, it was only marginal.According to the 2011 census report, the population growth rate was less than 2 per cent, i.e., 20/1000/year, a rate at which our population could increase rapidly.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: What principle do natural methods of contraception work on?
options: Avoiding chances of ovum and sperm meeting
questions.solution: Natural methods work on the principle of avoiding chances of ovum and sperms meeting. Periodic abstinence is one such method in which the couples avoid or abstain from coitus from day 10 to 17 of the menstrual cycle when ovulation could be expected. As chances of fertilisation are very high during this period, it is called the fertile period. Therefore, by abstaining from coitus during this period, conception could be prevented. Withdrawal or coitus interruptus is another method in which the male partner withdraws his penis from the vagina just before ejaculation so as to avoid insemination. Lactational amenorrhea (absence of menstruation) method is based on the fact that ovulation and therefore the cycle do not occur during the period of intense lactation following parturition. Therefore, as long as the mother breast-feeds the child fully, chances of conception are almost nil. However, this method has been reported to be effective only upto a maximum period of six months following parturition. As no medicines or devices are used in these methods, side effects are almost nil. Chances of failure, though, of this method are also high.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: What material are condoms typically made from?
questions.solution: Condomsare barriers made of thin rubber/ latex sheath that are used to cover the penis in the male or vagina and cervix in the female, just before coitus so that the ejaculated semen would not enter into the female reproductive tract. This can prevent conception. ‘Nirodh’ is a popular brand of condom for the male. Use of condoms has increased in recent years due to its additional benefit of protecting the user from contracting STIs and AIDS. Both the male and the female condoms are disposable, can be self-inserted and thereby gives privacy to the user. Diaphragms, cervical caps and vaults are also barriers made of rubber that are inserted into the female reproductive tract to cover the cervix during coitus. They prevent conception by blocking the entry of sperms through the cervix. They are reusable. Spermicidal creams, jellies and foams are usually used alongwith these barriers to increase their contraceptive efficiency

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Where are IntraUterine Devices (IUDs) inserted?
questions.solution: Another effective and popular method is the use of Intra Uterine Devices (IUDs). These devices are inserted by doctors or expert nurses in the uterus through vagina. These Intra Uterine Devices are presently available as the non-medicated IUDs (e.g., Lippes loop), copper releasing IUDs (CuT, Cu7, Multiload 375) and the hormone releasing IUDs (Progestasert, LNG-20). IUDs increase phagocytosis of sperms within the uterus and the Cu ions released suppress sperm motility and the fertilising capacity of sperms. The hormone releasing IUDs, in addition, make the uterus unsuitable for implantation and the cervix hostile to the sperms. IUDs are ideal contraceptives for the females who want to delay pregnancy and/or space children. It is one of most widely accepted methods of contraception in India.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: What do oral contraceptive pills contain?
questions.solution: Oral administration of small doses of either progestogens or progestogen–estrogen combinations is another contraceptive method used by the females. They are used in the form of tablets and hence are popularly called the pills. Pills have to be taken daily for a period of 21 days starting preferably within the first five days of menstrual cycle. After a gap of 7 days (during which menstruation occurs) it has to be repeated in the same pattern till the female desires to prevent conception. They inhibit ovulation and implantation as well as alter the quality of cervical mucus to prevent/retard entry of sperms. Pills are very effective with lesser side effects and are well accepted by the females. Saheli–the new oral contraceptive for the females contains a non-steroidal preparation. It is a ‘once a week’ pill with very few side effects and high contraceptive value.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: What are surgical methods of contraception also called?
questions.solution: Surgical methods, also called sterilisation, are generally advised for the male/female partner as a terminal method to prevent any more pregnancies. Surgical intervention blocks gamete transport and thereby prevent conception. Sterilisation procedure in the male is called ‘vasectomy’ and that in the female, ‘tubectomy’. In vasectomy, a small part of the vas deferens is removed or tied up through a small incision on the scrotum whereas in tubectomy, a small part of the fallopian tube is removed or tied up through a small incision in the abdomen or through vagina. These techniques are highly effective but their reversibility is very poor

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: What are some possible ill-effects of contraceptive methods?
options: Nausea, abdominal pain, breakthrough bleeding, irregular menstrual bleeding, breast cancer
questions.solution: It needs to be emphasised that the selection of a suitable contraceptive method and its use should always be undertaken in consultation with qualified medical professionals. One must also remember that contraceptives are not regular requirements for the maintenance of Reproductive Health. In fact, they are practiced against a natural reproductive event, i.e., conception/pregnancy. One is forced to use these methods either to prevent pregnancy or to delay or space pregnancy due to personal reasons. No doubt, the widespread use of these methods have a significant role in checking uncontrolled growth of population. However, their possible ill-effects like nausea, abdominal pain, breakthrough bleeding, irregular menstrual bleeding or even breast cancer, though not very significant, should not be totally ignored.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: What is the term for the intentional or voluntary termination of pregnancy before full term?
questions.solution: Intentional or voluntary termination of pregnancy before full term is called medical termination of pregnancy (MTP) or induced abortion. Nearly 45 to 50 million MTPs are performed in a year all over the world which accounts to 1/5th of the total number of conceived pregnancies in a year. Whether to accept / legalise MTP or not is being debated upon in many countries due to emotional, ethical, religious and social issues involved in it. Government of India legalised MTP in 1971 with some strict conditions to avoid its misuse. Such restrictions are all the more important to check indiscriminate and illegal female foeticides which are reported to be high in India.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: What is the definition of infertility?
options: Inability to engage in sexual activity
Inability to produce children in spite of unprotected sexual cohabitation
questions.solution: A discussion on Reproductive Health is incomplete without a mention of infertility. A large number of couples all over the world including India are infertile, i.e., they are unable to produce children inspite of unprotected sexual co-habitation. The reasons for this could be many–physical, congenital, diseases, drugs, immunological or even psychological. In India, often the female is blamed for the couple being childless, but more often than not, the problem lies in the male partner. Specialised health care units (infertility clinics, etc.) could help in diagnosis and corrective treatment of some of these disorders and enable these couples to have children. However, where such corrections are not possible, the couples could be assisted to have children through certain special techniques commonly known as assisted reproductive technologies (ART).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: What does IVF stand for in the context of assisted reproductive technologies?
questions.solution: In vitro fertilisation (IVF–fertilisation outside the body in almost similar conditions as that in the body) followed by embryo transfer (ET) is one of such methods. In this method, popularly known as test tube baby programme, ova from the wife/donor (female) and sperms from the husband/donor (male) are collected and are induced to form zygote under simulated conditions in the laboratory. The zygote or early embryos (with upto 8 blastomeres) could then be transferred into the fallopian tube (ZIFT–zygote intra fallopian transfer) and embryos with more than 8 blastomeres, into the uterus (IUT – intra uterine transfer), to complete its further development. Embryos formed by in-vivo fertilisation (fusion of gametes within the female) also could be used for such transfer to assist those females who cannot conceive.

In this method, popularly known as test tube baby programme, ova from the wife/donor (female) and sperms from the husband/donor (male) are collected and are induced to form zygote under simulated conditions in the laboratory. The zygote or early embryos (with upto 8 blastomeres) could then be transferred into the fallopian tube (ZIFT–zygote intra fallopian transfer) and embryos with more than 8 blastomeres, into the uterus (IUT – intra uterine transfer), to complete its further development. Embryos formed by in-vivo fertilisation (fusion of gametes within the female) also could be used for such transfer to assist those females who cannot conceive.

questions.q: Why are the benefits of these techniques limited to a few people?
questions.solution: Though options are many, all these techniques require extremely high precision handling by specialised professionals and expensive instrumentation. Therefore, these facilities are presently available only in very few centres in the country. Obviously their benefits is affordable to only a limited number of people. Emotional, religious and social factors are also deterrents in the adoption of these methods. Since the ultimate aim of all these procedures is to have children, in India we have so many orphaned and destitute children, who would probably not survive till maturity, unless taken care of. Our laws permit legal adoption and it is as yet, one of the best methods for couples looking for parenthood.

questions.solution:

In vitro methodsFeatures
A. Test tube baby1. Form an embryo in the laboratory in which a sperm is directly injected into the ovum.
B. IUT2. The zygote or early embryos (with upto 8 blastomeres) could then be transferred into the fallopian tube
C. ZIFT3. Embryos with more than 8 blastomeres, are transferred into the uterus

questions.solution:
In this method, popularly known as test tube baby programme, ova from the wife/donor (female) and sperms from the husband/donor (male) are collected and are induced to form zygote under simulated conditions in the laboratory. The zygote or early embryos (with upto 8 blastomeres) could then be transferred into the fallopian tube (ZIFT–zygote intra fallopian transfer) and embryos with more than 8 blastomeres, into the uterus (IUT – intra uterine transfer), to complete its further developmen
Intra cytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI) is another specialised procedure to form an embryo in the laboratory in which a sperm is directly injected into the ovum.

It releases copper ions that suppress sperm motility and the fertilising capacity of sperms.
It makes the uterus unsuitable for implantation and the cervix hostile to sperms.

questions.solution:

(iii) Trichomoniasis

questions.solution:

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: A married couple seeks medical advice for infertility. Clinical evaluation reveals that the male partner has a very low sperm count in his ejaculates. The female partner has bilaterally blocked fallopian tubes, but her uterus is normal and capable of supporting a pregnancy. Which of the following Assisted Reproductive Technologies (ART) is the most appropriate and viable option for this couple?
options: Intra Cytoplasmic Sperm Injection (ICSI) followed by Intra Uterine Transfer (IUT)
In-vitro fertilisation (IVF) followed by Zygote Intra Fallopian Transfer (ZIFT)
questions.solution:
The male partner has a very low sperm count, which typically requires Artificial Insemination (AI), Intra-uterine insemination (IUI), or Intra Cytoplasmic Sperm Injection (ICSI).

However, the female partner has bilaterally blocked fallopian tubes. This anatomical barrier prevents natural in-vivo fertilisation, meaning AI, IUI, and Gamete Intra Fallopian Transfer (GIFT) will be unsuccessful because the sperm and ovum cannot meet.

Furthermore, Zygote Intra Fallopian Transfer (ZIFT) is not viable because the early embryo cannot be transferred into blocked tubes.

The only viable option is to perform in-vitro fertilisation using ICSI (to overcome the low sperm count) and then transfer the resulting embryo directly into the normal uterus via Intra Uterine Transfer (IUT), completely bypassing the blocked fallopian tubes.

Answer: Intra Cytoplasmic Sperm Injection (ICSI) followed by Intra Uterine Transfer (IUT)

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following options correctly identifies the contraceptive method, its category, and its corresponding mechanism of action?
options: Cervical caps - Barrier method - Inhibits ovulation
Coitus interruptus - Natural method - Prevents spermatogenesis
Copper T - Barrier method - Suppresses sperm motility
Tubectomy - Surgical method - Blocks gamete transport
questions.solution:
Tubectomy is a surgical method (sterilisation) in females where a small part of the fallopian tube is removed or tied up. This blocks gamete transport and thereby prevents conception.

Cervical caps are barrier methods but they do not inhibit ovulation; they prevent conception by blocking the entry of sperms through the cervix.

Coitus interruptus is a natural method that prevents insemination by withdrawal of the penis just before ejaculation, but it does not halt spermatogenesis.

Copper T suppresses sperm motility and the fertilising capacity of sperms, but it is an Intra Uterine Device (IUD), not a barrier method.

Answer: Tubectomy - Surgical method - Blocks gamete transport

Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Surgical methods of contraception are highly effective but their reversibility is very poor.
Reason (R): Surgical intervention blocks gamete transport and thereby prevents conception.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is correct but Reason (R) is not correct.
Assertion (A) is not correct but Reason (R) is correct.
questions.solution:
Surgical methods (sterilisation such as vasectomy and tubectomy) are highly effective terminal methods of contraception, but their reversibility is very poor due to surgical complexity and tissue scarring. Thus, Assertion (A) is correct.

The mechanism of action of these methods is the physical blockage of gamete transport, which prevents conception. Thus, Reason (R) is also correct.

However, while the blockage of gamete transport explains why these methods are highly effective at preventing pregnancy, it does not explain why the surgical reversibility is poor. Therefore, both (A) and (R) are correct, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

Answer: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

questions.q:
A pregnant woman with a family history of a severe genetic disorder is advised to undergo a diagnostic test. The doctor extracts a small amount of the fluid surrounding the developing embryo to check for the disorder.

Identify the procedure, the specific biological component analysed to detect the disorder, and the primary reason this procedure is legally restricted in India.
options: Amniocentesis ; Dissolved maternal hormones ; To prevent female foeticide
Chorionic villus sampling ; Foetal cells ; To prevent medical termination of pregnancy
Amniocentesis ; Foetal cells for chromosomal pattern ; To check maternal mortality rate
Amniocentesis ; Foetal cells for chromosomal pattern ; To prevent female foeticide
questions.solution:
The procedure described is amniocentesis, in which some of the amniotic fluid surrounding the developing embryo is extracted.

The fluid is used to analyse the foetal cells and dissolved substances to determine the chromosomal pattern, which helps in detecting genetic disorders such as Down syndrome, haemophilia, and sickle-cell anemia. It does not analyse maternal hormones for this purpose.

The procedure is legally restricted (through a statutory ban on sex determination) to check the increasing menace of female foeticides.

Answer: Amniocentesis ; Foetal cells for chromosomal pattern ; To prevent female foeticide

questions.solution:
ZIFT stands for Zygote Intra Fallopian Transfer.

Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Intra-uterine insemination (IUI) is not a suitable treatment for females with bilaterally blocked fallopian tubes, even if the male partner has a very low sperm count.
Reason (R): IUI involves artificially introducing semen into the uterus, which requires at least one patent (open) fallopian tube for in-vivo fertilization to occur.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
questions.solution:
Intra-uterine insemination (IUI) is an in-vivo fertilization technique where semen is artificially introduced into the uterus to assist couples where the male partner has a low sperm count. For fertilization to occur naturally, the sperm must swim up from the uterus into the ampullary region of the fallopian tube to meet the ovum. If the fallopian tubes are bilaterally blocked, the sperm cannot reach the ovum, making IUI ineffective. Therefore, both Assertion and Reason are true, and the Reason correctly explains the Assertion.

Answer: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)

A female patient consults a doctor for a contraceptive method. She prefers a method that is reusable, made of rubber, and needs to be inserted into the reproductive tract to cover the cervix during coitus.

Which of the following contraceptive methods matches her requirement, and to which category does it belong?
questions.solution:
According to NCERT, diaphragms, cervical caps, and vaults are barrier methods made of rubber that are inserted into the female reproductive tract to cover the cervix during coitus. A key feature of these specific barriers is that they are reusable.

Female condoms are also barrier methods made of rubber/latex, but they are disposable, not reusable.

Lippes loop is a non-medicated Intra Uterine Device (IUD) inserted into the uterus, not a rubber barrier covering the cervix.

Implants are hormone-containing devices placed under the skin, not surgical sterilization methods or cervical barriers.

Therefore, 'Vaults' correctly match the description of a reusable rubber barrier method.

Answer: Vaults – Barrier method

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: A female patient is taking a combined progestogen-estrogen oral contraceptive pill to prevent pregnancy. The continuous exogenous supply of these hormones exerts a negative feedback effect on the anterior pituitary. As a direct consequence, which of the following critical endocrine events is primarily inhibited?
options: Surge of progesterone from the corpus luteum
Secretion of oxytocin from the posterior pituitary
Rapid decline of estrogen leading to menstruation
questions.solution:
Combined oral contraceptive pills contain synthetic progestogen and estrogen. The continuous presence of these exogenous hormones in the blood exerts a negative feedback effect on the hypothalamus and anterior pituitary gland.

This negative feedback suppresses the secretion of gonadotropins (FSH and LH). Consequently, the pre-ovulatory surge of Luteinizing Hormone (LH), which is the essential trigger for ovulation, is inhibited. Without ovulation, conception cannot occur.

The surge of progesterone from the corpus luteum does not occur because the corpus luteum is never formed, but this is a secondary consequence of anovulation, not the primary event inhibited by the pituitary feedback. Oxytocin is not involved in this mechanism, and the pills actually prevent the endogenous cycle rather than inhibiting the decline of estrogen.

Answer: Pre-ovulatory surge of Luteinizing Hormone (LH)

questions.q:
Consider the following two cases of infertility:
Case A: A female who cannot produce an ovum but can provide a suitable environment for fertilization and further development.
Case B: A couple where the male partner has a very low sperm count in the ejaculates, while the female partner is completely normal.

Which of the following pairs of Assisted Reproductive Technologies (ART) is the most appropriate for Case A and Case B, respectively?
questions.solution:
According to NCERT, for a female who cannot produce an ovum but can provide a suitable environment for fertilization and further development, the recommended technique is Gamete Intra Fallopian Transfer (GIFT), where an ovum from a donor is transferred to her fallopian tube.

For a male partner with a very low sperm count, the condition can be corrected by Artificial Insemination (AI), such as Intra-uterine insemination (IUI), where semen collected from the husband or a donor is artificially introduced into the uterus of the female.

Therefore, GIFT and IUI are the most appropriate techniques for Case A and Case B, respectively. ZIFT and IUT are incorrect for Case A because they involve the transfer of an embryo, not a gamete.

Answer: GIFT and IUI

questions.q: A woman who recently delivered a baby is exclusively breastfeeding and relies on the absence of her menstrual cycle to prevent pregnancy. Identify the specific name of this natural contraceptive method and the maximum period following parturition for which it is considered highly effective.
options: Lactational amenorrhea; up to six months
Lactational amenorrhea; up to twelve months
Periodic abstinence; up to six months
Safe period method; up to three months
questions.solution:
Lactational amenorrhea is a natural method of contraception based on the absence of menstruation and ovulation during the period of intense lactation following parturition.

According to NCERT, as long as the mother breastfeeds the child fully, chances of conception are almost nil. However, this method has been reported to be effective only up to a maximum period of six months following parturition.

Periodic abstinence and safe period methods involve avoiding coitus during the fertile period of the menstrual cycle, which does not match the scenario of a lactating mother experiencing amenorrhea.

Answer: Lactational amenorrhea; up to six months

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Read the following statements carefully:

Statement I: Early symptoms of most STIs are minor and include itching, fluid discharge, slight pain, and swellings in the genital region.
Statement II: Infected females may often be asymptomatic and hence, may remain undetected for long.
Statement III: STIs do not lead to severe complications like ectopic pregnancies or infertility.
Statement IV: All sexually transmitted infections are completely curable if detected early.

Which of the following combinations of statements is correct?
questions.solution:
Statement I is correct as early symptoms of most STIs are indeed minor and include itching, fluid discharge, slight pain, and swellings in the genital region.

Statement II is correct because infected females may often be asymptomatic, leading to delayed detection.

Statement III is incorrect because if STIs remain untreated, they can lead to severe complications later, including pelvic inflammatory diseases (PID), abortions, stillbirths, ectopic pregnancies, infertility, or even cancer of the reproductive tract.

Statement IV is incorrect because not all STIs are curable; Hepatitis-B, genital herpes, and HIV infections are not completely curable.

Thus, only Statements I and II are correct.

Answer: Statements I and II

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: A couple is seeking medical help for infertility. Clinical evaluations reveal that the female partner has normal reproductive functions, but the male partner has a very low sperm count in his ejaculates. Which of the following assisted reproductive technologies is explicitly recommended to correct this specific condition?
questions.solution:
According to NCERT, infertility cases arising either due to the inability of the male partner to inseminate the female or due to very low sperm counts in the ejaculates (oligospermia) can be corrected by the Artificial insemination (AI) technique.

In this technique, the semen collected either from the husband or a healthy donor is artificially introduced either into the vagina or into the uterus (IUI) of the female.

Gamete intra fallopian transfer (GIFT) is recommended for females who cannot produce an ovum. Zygote intra fallopian transfer (ZIFT) and Embryo transfer (ET) are steps in in vitro fertilization (IVF) programmes, which are more complex and not the primary recommendation for isolated low sperm count when the female is entirely normal.

Answer: Artificial insemination (AI)

Therefore, the correct matching is (A)-(III), (B)-(I), (C)-(IV), (D)-(II).

questions.q:
Consider the following Assisted Reproductive Technologies (ART):
(a) ZIFT
(b) IUT
(c) GIFT
(d) ICSI
(e) AI
(f) IUI

How many of the above procedures involve fertilization outside the body of the female?
questions.solution:
Fertilization outside the body of the female in almost similar conditions as that in the body is called in-vitro fertilization (IVF).

Among the given procedures:
- ZIFT (Zygote Intra Fallopian Transfer) involves IVF followed by the transfer of the zygote or early embryo into the fallopian tube.
- IUT (Intra Uterine Transfer) involves IVF followed by the transfer of embryos with more than 8 blastomeres into the uterus.
- ICSI (Intra Cytoplasmic Sperm Injection) is a specialized IVF procedure where a sperm is directly injected into the ovum.

GIFT (Gamete Intra Fallopian Transfer), AI (Artificial Insemination), and IUI (Intra-uterine insemination) all involve in-vivo fertilization (fertilization inside the female body).

Therefore, exactly three procedures (ZIFT, IUT, and ICSI) involve in-vitro fertilization.

Answer: Three

questions.q: Which of the following statements correctly describes the biological basis and the legal status of amniocentesis in India?
options: It analyses the chromosomal pattern of foetal cells in the amniotic fluid and is legally permitted for detecting certain genetic disorders.
It analyses maternal blood cells to detect genetic disorders and is completely banned in India for all purposes.

It analyses the dissolved substances in the amniotic fluid but is completely banned in India for all purposes to check female foeticide.
questions.solution:
Amniocentesis involves taking some of the amniotic fluid of the developing foetus to analyse the foetal cells and dissolved substances. It is based on the chromosomal pattern in the amniotic fluid surrounding the developing embryo.

It is legally permitted and used to test for the presence of certain genetic disorders such as Down's syndrome, haemophilia, and sickle-cell anaemia.

However, there is a statutory ban on amniocentesis for sex determination to legally check the increasing menace of female foeticide. It is not completely banned for all purposes, nor does it analyse maternal blood cells. It is also not promoted as an RCH strategy for sex determination.

Thus, the statement describing it as analysing the chromosomal pattern of foetal cells in the amniotic fluid and being legally permitted for detecting certain genetic disorders is completely correct.

Answer: It analyses the chromosomal pattern of foetal cells in the amniotic fluid and is legally permitted for detecting certain genetic disorders.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: A married couple seeks medical help for infertility. Clinical evaluation reveals that the female partner has normal, patent fallopian tubes and a normal uterus, but her ovaries fail to produce viable ova. The male partner has a normal sperm count and normal sperm motility. Which of the following Assisted Reproductive Technologies (ART) is the most suitable for this couple?
questions.solution:
The female partner cannot produce ova but can provide a suitable environment for fertilization and further embryonic development, as her fallopian tubes and uterus are normal. The male partner has normal sperm parameters.

In such cases, the most suitable technique is GIFT (Gamete Intra Fallopian Transfer). An ovum collected from a donor is transferred into the fallopian tube of the female, allowing in-vivo fertilization by the male partner's sperms.

ZIFT and ICSI involve in-vitro fertilization, which is unnecessary here since natural in-vivo fertilization is possible. IUI (Intra Uterine Insemination) is used when the male partner has a low sperm count or inability to inseminate, which is not the case here.

Answer: GIFT

questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Lactational amenorrhea is considered a highly effective contraceptive method for up to two years following parturition.

Reason (R): Intense lactation causes high levels of prolactin which suppresses gonadotropin secretion, thereby preventing ovulation.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is incorrect because according to NCERT, lactational amenorrhea is effective only up to a maximum period of six months following parturition, not two years.

Reason (R) is correct because intense lactation stimulates high secretion of prolactin, which in turn suppresses the release of gonadotropins (LH and FSH) from the pituitary. This prevents the menstrual cycle and ovulation.

Therefore, Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.

Answer: Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: An embryo formed by in-vitro fertilization has developed to the 16-blastomere stage. Which of the following correctly identifies the assisted reproductive technique and the specific anatomical site where this embryo should be transferred?
questions.solution:
According to NCERT, in Embryo Transfer (ET) techniques, the zygote or early embryos with up to 8 blastomeres are transferred into the fallopian tube (ZIFT - Zygote Intra Fallopian Transfer). Embryos with more than 8 blastomeres are transferred into the uterus (IUT - Intra Uterine Transfer) to complete their further development.

Since the embryo in question has 16 blastomeres (which is greater than the 8-cell threshold), the correct technique is IUT and the anatomical site of transfer is the uterus. Selecting ZIFT or the fallopian tube represents a confusion of the blastomere count limits for each specific transfer site.

Answer: IUT, Uterus

Assertion : Foetal disorders can be diagnosed by chorionic villi sampling.
Reason : Karyotyping can be done for mitotically dividing cells of chorionic villi.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.
If assertion is true but reason is false.
If both assertion and reason are false.
questions.solution: During early pregnancy, foetal disorders can be diagnosed using chorionic villi sampling. In this technique the physician inserts a narrow, flexible tube through the mother's vagina and cervix into the uterus (guided by ultrasound) and withdraws a small amount of foetal tissue (chorionic villi) from the placenta. Because the cells of the chorionic villi are undergoing rapid mitosis, these cells can be used for karyotyping.

questions.q: In assisted reproductive technology where gametes have been fertilized in vitro, which of the following is practicable for embryo transplantation in Fallopian tube?
options: Only embryo up to 8 blastomeres if zygote is not transplanted.
Only zygote is transplanted not embryo
Either embryo or zygote with 8 blastomere phase transplanted.
Morulla with 8-24 celled stage is transplanted in Fallopian tube.
questions.solution: In in vitro fertilization (IVF-fertilization outside the body in almost similar conditions as that in the body) followed by embryo transfer (ET), ova from the wife/donor (female) and sperms from the husband/donor (male) are collected and are induced to form zygote under simulated conditions in the laboratory. The zygote or early embryos (with upto 8 blastomeres) could then be transferred into the Fallopian tube (ZIFT-Zygote Intra Fallopian Transfer) and embryos with more than 8 blastomeres, into the uterus (IUT-Intra Uterine Transfer), to complete its further development.

Assertion : Now-a-days amniocentesis is banned.
Reason : Amniocentesis gives the information of any abnormality in the foetus and many other complications regarding pregnancy can be detected.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion
If assertion is true but reason is false
If both assertion and reason are false.
questions.solution: Amniocentesis is a foetal sex determination and disorder test based on the chromosomal pattern in the amniotic fluid surrounding the developing embryo. The amniotic fluid contains cells from foetus skin and respiratory tract. These cells are cultured and are used to determine chromosomal abnormalities (Down's syndrome, Klinefelter's syndrome, etc.) and metabolic disorders (phenylketonuria, sickle cell anaemia, etc.) of the foetus. But now-a-days instead of positive uses of amniocentesis it is being used for female foeticide. Sex of the foetus is determined using amniocentesis and then if it turns out to been a female one, foetus is aborted. That is why amniocentesis has been banned in India.

questions.solution: (b) : Amniocentesis is a foetal sex determination and disorder test based on the chromosomal pattern in the amniotic fluid surrounding the developing embryo.
